questions.question: When driving in fog, which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and turn on your flashers and low beam headlights. Do not use high beams.

questions.question: Which is required emergency equipment for a commercial vehicle?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: A driver with a baffled tank should be most careful about:
questions.explanation: Baffles stop forward and backward surge, but they do not stop side-to-side surge. Side-to-side movement can cause the vehicle to roll over.

questions.question: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After starting, the coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating level.

questions.question: How can you help prevent surge in a tank?

options.text: Brake well in advance to avoid sudden stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake well in advance to avoid sudden stops.
questions.explanation: To reduce surge risk, brake early and increase your following distance. This helps you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ makes steering difficult.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play (about 2 inches on a 20-inch wheel). More than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: A skid caused by over-acceleration can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Simply lift your foot off the accelerator to fix an over-acceleration skid. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: When making a quick stop while carrying liquids, use the:
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles are less stable and can roll over or skid easily. Use the controlled braking method for emergency stops with liquid cargo.

questions.question: To use stab braking with liquid cargo, apply the brakes by:

options.text: Using about half your normal force.
Applying as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Pressing completely until wheels lock. Release until wheels roll, then repeat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressing completely until wheels lock. Release until wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means fully pressing the brakes until they lock. Release until the wheels start rolling, then repeat.

questions.question: In very hot weather, if your tire air pressure is too high, you should:

options.text: Let the tires cool before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the tires cool before driving.
questions.explanation: Air expands in heat, which can make tire pressure dangerously high. Stop and let tires cool. Do not release air, or pressure may drop too much when they cool.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does it mean if other vehicles' tires are not spraying water?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is trapped under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: When driving in wet conditions, no water spray from other tires means ice has formed on the road. Be very careful when it is wet and cold.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails, what happens?

options.text: The truck can only drive slowly.

questions.explanation: ABS is an added safety feature. It stops brakes from locking during hard braking. If ABS fails, the basic brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: How often should you use your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Only if someone helps you watch blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors on both sides of your vehicle often while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to drive off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: If stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call 911 or the emergency number listed.

questions.question: How must hazard placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: Within three inches of other markings.
So words and numbers read left to right.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be at least three inches away from other markings. They must be level and readable from left to right.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain why you check each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you check each item.
questions.explanation: During the inspection test, you must do a full vehicle inspection. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: What must a truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: What is true about broken suspension parts?
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are extremely dangerous.

questions.question: When must you stop quickly while carrying liquid cargo, which method is best?
questions.explanation: Use the stab braking method if you must stop quickly to avoid an accident while carrying liquid cargo. Quick steering while braking can cause your vehicle to tip, especially if it has a high center of gravity.

questions.question: When should you slow down and be extra careful?
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in and around work zones, where the road edge drops off sharply, when objects are on the road, and on freeway on- and off-ramps.
